verses.1:1: The word of the LORD which came to Joel, the son of Pethuel.
verses.1:2: Hear this, O elders, and give ear, all inhabitants of the land: Has this happened in your days, or even in the days of your fathers?
verses.1:3: Recount it to your children, and let your children tell their children, and their children to another generation.
verses.1:4: What the shearing locust left, the swarming locust has eaten; and what the swarming locust left, the young locust has eaten; and what the young locust left, the devouring locust has eaten.
verses.1:5: Awake, O drunkards, and weep; wail, all who drink wine, over the sweet wine, because it has been cut off from your mouth.
verses.1:6: For a nation has come up against my land, mighty and beyond number; its teeth are the teeth of a lion, and it has the fangs of a fierce lion.
verses.1:7: It has turned my vine into a desolation and my fig tree into splinters; it has stripped it completely bare and cast it aside; its branches have turned white.
verses.1:8: Lament like a virgin girded with sackcloth for the husband of her youth.
verses.1:9: The grain offering and the drink offering have been cut off from the house of the LORD; the priests, the ministers of the LORD, mourn.
verses.1:10: The field is devastated, the ground mourns; for the grain is laid waste, the new wine has dried up, and the fresh oil languishes.
verses.1:11: Be put to shame, O plowmen; wail, O vinedressers, over the wheat and over the barley, for the harvest of the field has perished.
verses.1:12: The vine has dried up, and the fig tree has languished; the pomegranate, the palm also, and the apple tree—all the trees of the field are withered; indeed, gladness has withered away from the sons of men.
verses.1:13: Gird yourselves and lament, O priests; wail, O ministers of the altar. Come, pass the night in sackcloth, O ministers of my God, for the grain offering and the drink offering are withheld from the house of your God.
verses.1:14: Consecrate a fast, proclaim a solemn assembly; gather the elders and all the inhabitants of the land to the house of the LORD your God, and cry out to the LORD.
verses.1:15: Alas for the day! For the day of the LORD is near, and like destruction from the Almighty it shall come.
verses.1:16: Has not the food been cut off before our very eyes, and joy and gladness from the house of our God?
verses.1:17: The seeds shrivel beneath their clods; the storehouses lie desolate, and the granaries are broken down, for the grain has withered.
verses.1:18: How the beasts groan! The herds of cattle wander in perplexity because there is no pasture for them; even the flocks of sheep suffer punishment.
verses.1:19: To You, O LORD, I cry out; for fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness, and flame has scorched all the trees of the field.
verses.1:20: Even the beasts of the field pant after You, for the streams of water have dried up, and fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness.
verses.2:1: Blow a trumpet in Zion, and sound an alarm on My holy mountain! Let all the inhabitants of the land tremble, for the day of the LORD is coming, for it is near.
verses.2:2: A day of darkness and deep gloom, a day of clouds and thick darkness! Like the dawn spread over the mountains, a great and mighty people; there has never been the like of them from of old, nor shall there be again after them, through the years of generation after generation.
verses.2:3: A fire devours before them, and behind them a flame blazes; the land is like the garden of Eden before them, and behind them a desolate wilderness, and surely nothing escapes them.
verses.2:4: Their appearance is like the appearance of horses, and like horsemen, so they run.
verses.2:5: Like the noise of chariots they leap upon the tops of the mountains, like the sound of a flame of fire devouring stubble, like a mighty people arrayed for battle.
verses.2:6: Before them the peoples are in anguish; all faces turn pale.
verses.2:7: Like mighty men they run; like men of war they scale the wall. Each one marches in his own course, and they do not swerve from their paths.
verses.2:8: They do not jostle one another; every man marches along his own highway. Though they plunge through the weapons, they are not cut off.
verses.2:9: They rush upon the city, they run along the wall, they climb up into the houses; they enter through the windows like a thief.
verses.2:10: The earth quakes before them, the heavens tremble; the sun and the moon grow dark, and the stars withdraw their brightness.
verses.2:11: And the LORD utters His voice before His army, for His camp is exceedingly great, and mighty is the one who executes His word. For the day of the LORD is great and exceedingly fearsome, and who can endure it?
verses.2:12: "Yet even now," declares the LORD, "return to Me with all your heart, with fasting, with weeping, and with mourning."
verses.2:13: And rend your heart and not your garments, and return to the LORD your God, for He is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and abundant in lovingkindness, and He relents concerning calamity.
verses.2:14: Who knows whether He will turn and relent, and leave a blessing behind Him—a grain offering and a drink offering for the LORD your God?
verses.2:15: Blow a trumpet in Zion, consecrate a fast, proclaim a solemn assembly.
verses.2:16: Gather the people, sanctify the congregation, assemble the elders, gather the little children and those who nurse at the breast; let the bridegroom go forth from his chamber, and the bride from her canopy.
verses.2:17: Between the vestibule and the altar let the priests, the ministers of the LORD, weep; and let them say, "Spare Your people, O LORD, and do not give Your heritage to reproach, that the nations should rule over them. Why should they say among the peoples, 'Where is their God?'"
verses.2:18: Then the LORD became zealous for His land and had compassion upon His people.
verses.2:19: The LORD answered and said to His people, "Behold, I am sending you the grain, the new wine, and the fresh oil, and you shall be satisfied with them; and I will no longer make you a reproach among the nations.
verses.2:20: I will remove the northerner far from you and drive him into a parched and desolate land, his vanguard into the eastern sea and his rear guard into the western sea; and his stench shall rise, and his foul odor shall ascend, for he has done great things.
verses.2:21: Do not fear, O land; be glad and rejoice, for the LORD has done great things!
verses.2:22: Do not fear, O beasts of the field, for the pastures of the wilderness have grown green; for the tree bears its fruit, and the fig tree and the vine yield their full strength.
verses.2:23: And you children of Zion, be glad and rejoice in the LORD your God; for He has given you the early rain in righteousness, and He has poured down for you the rain—the early rain and the latter rain—in the first month.
verses.2:24: The threshing floors shall be filled with grain, and the vats shall overflow with new wine and fresh oil.
verses.2:25: And I will restore to you the years that the swarming locust has eaten—the creeping locust, the stripping locust, and the gnawing locust—My great army which I sent among you.
verses.2:26: You shall eat in abundance and be satisfied, and praise the name of the LORD your God, who has dealt wondrously with you; and My people shall never be put to shame.
verses.2:27: Then you shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the LORD your God and there is no other; and My people shall never be put to shame."
verses.3:1: And it shall be afterward that I will pour out My Spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions.
verses.3:2: And even upon the manservants and upon the maidservants in those days I will pour out My Spirit.
verses.3:3: And I will display wonders in the heavens and on the earth: blood and fire and columns of smoke.
verses.3:4: The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the coming of the great and fearsome day of the LORD.
verses.3:5: And it shall be that everyone who calls upon the name of the LORD shall be delivered; for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there shall be deliverance, as the LORD has spoken, and among the survivors whom the LORD calls.
verses.4:1: For behold, in those days and at that time, when I turn back the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem,
verses.4:2: I will assemble all the nations and bring them down into the Valley of Jehoshaphat; and there I will enter into judgment with them concerning My people and My inheritance Israel, whom they scattered among the nations, and My land they divided.
verses.4:3: And for My people they cast lots; they gave a boy for a harlot, and sold a girl for wine, and drank.
verses.4:4: Moreover, what are you to Me, O Tyre and Sidon, and all the regions of Philistia? Are you rendering a recompense to Me? And if you are retaliating against Me, swiftly and speedily I will return your recompense upon your own head.
verses.4:5: Because you have taken My silver and My gold, and have brought My finest treasures into your temples;
verses.4:6: and the children of Judah and the children of Jerusalem you have sold to the Greeks, so as to remove them far from their border.
verses.4:7: Behold, I am rousing them from the place to which you sold them, and I will return your recompense upon your own head.
verses.4:8: And I will sell your sons and your daughters into the hand of the children of Judah, and they will sell them to the Sabeans, to a distant nation; for the LORD has spoken.
verses.4:9: Proclaim this among the nations: Consecrate war! Rouse the mighty men! Let all the men of war draw near; let them come up.
verses.4:10: Hammer your plowshares into swords and your pruning hooks into spears; let the weak one say, "I am a mighty man."
verses.4:11: Hasten and come, all you nations on every side, and gather yourselves together. There bring down Your mighty ones, O LORD!
verses.4:12: Let the nations be roused and come up to the Valley of Jehoshaphat; for there I will sit to judge all the nations on every side.
verses.4:13: Thrust in the sickle, for the harvest has ripened. Come, tread, for the winepress is full; the vats overflow, for great is their wickedness.
verses.4:14: Multitudes, multitudes in the Valley of Decision! For near is the day of the LORD in the Valley of Decision.
verses.4:15: The sun and the moon grow dark, and the stars withdraw their radiance.
verses.4:16: And the LORD will roar from Zion, and from Jerusalem He will utter His voice, and the heavens and the earth will quake; yet the LORD is a refuge for His people and a stronghold for the children of Israel.
verses.4:17: Then you shall know that I am the LORD your God, who dwells in Zion, My holy mountain; and Jerusalem shall be holy, and strangers shall pass through her no more.
verses.4:18: And it shall come to pass in that day that the mountains shall drip with sweet wine, and the hills shall flow with milk, and all the streambeds of Judah shall run with water; and a fountain shall go forth from the house of the LORD and water the Valley of Shittim.
verses.4:19: Egypt shall become a desolation, and Edom shall become a wilderness of desolation, on account of the violence done against the children of Judah, because they have shed innocent blood in their land.
verses.4:20: Yet Judah shall be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.
verses.4:21: And I will cleanse their blood which I have not cleansed; and the LORD dwells in Zion.

notes.1:4: The four Hebrew locust terms (gazam, arbeh, yeleq, and chasil) represent either successive stages of locust development or relentless waves of devastation.
notes.1:6: "My land" here (and "my vine" and "my fig tree" in v. 7) may be understood either as the prophet speaking of his own homeland or as the LORD speaking of His covenant land.
notes.1:12: Across verses 10–12, the Hebrew weaves a wordplay between nearly identical forms of the roots meaning "to dry up" (yavesh) and "to be put to shame" (bosh).
notes.1:15: "Like destruction from the Almighty" renders the striking Hebrew assonance ke-shod mi-Shadday.
notes.2:6: The rare Hebrew idiom qibbetsu fa'rur (cf. Nahum 2:10) literally speaks of faces gathering a flush or pallor, expressing sudden terror.
notes.2:17: The Hebrew verb mashal here may mean either "rule over" or "make a byword of" among the nations.
notes.2:20: The clause "for he has done great things" portrays the northern invader's arrogant presumption and stands in deliberate contrast to the same Hebrew phrase applied to the LORD in v. 21.
notes.2:23: Hebrew ha-moreh ("the early rain") can also mean "the teacher," yielding an alternate reading "the teacher of righteousness," though the parallel clause favors autumn rain; "in the first month" translates Hebrew ba-rishon ("in the first").
notes.3:1: In the Masoretic Text, Joel 3 consists of five verses (3:1–5), corresponding to Joel 2:28–32 in most English Bibles.
notes.3:2: The Masoretic Text reads "the manservants and the maidservants" without a possessive pronoun, unlike the Septuagint and Acts 2:18 ("My servants").
notes.4:1: The Hebrew Qere reads the causative form meaning "I turn back" or "I restore," whereas the Ketiv reads the simple stem. The idiom "turn back the captivity" can also signify restoring the fortunes; Joel chapter 4 in the Masoretic Hebrew corresponds to chapter 3 in most English Bibles.
notes.4:2: The name Jehoshaphat means "the LORD judges," underscoring the scene of universal judgment in this valley, which is also called the Valley of Decision in verse 14.
notes.4:9: "Consecrate war" reflects the ancient Near Eastern and Israelite custom of ritual sanctification and sacrificial preparation prior to battle.
notes.4:18: "The Valley of Shittim" literally means "the Valley of Acacias," evoking an arid valley transformed by the waters issuing from the temple of the LORD.
notes.4:21: The Masoretic Hebrew uses the verb meaning "cleanse" or "acquit" (clearing from bloodguilt), whereas some ancient versions such as the Septuagint read a similar Hebrew root meaning "avenge."
